sanskrit: aṣṭau pūrvanimittāni narasya vinaśiṣyataḥ brāhmaṇān prathamaṃ dveṣṭi brāhmaṇaiś ca virudhyate
english: There are eight forewarning signs of a man who is about to perish: first, he hates brahmins, and he quarrels with brahmins.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇasvāni cādatte brāhmaṇāṃś ca jighāṃsati ramate nindayā caiṣāṃ praśaṃsāṃ nābhinandati
english: He seizes the property of brahmins, he desires to slay brahmins, he takes delight in reviling them and does not rejoice in their praise.

sanskrit: naitān smarati kṛtyeṣu yācitaś cābhyasūyati etān doṣān naraḥ prājño buddhyā buddhvā vivarjayet
english: He does not think of them in times of duty, and when asked he responds with envy. A wise man, having understood these faults with his intelligence, should abandon them.

sanskrit: aṣṭāv imāni harṣasya navanītāni bhārata vartamānāni dṛśyante tāny eva susukhāny api
english: O Bharata, these eight are the fresh butter of joy — they are seen to be present in life, and each one brings great happiness.

sanskrit: samāgamaś ca sakhibhir mahāṃś caiva dhanāgamaḥ putreṇa ca pariṣvaṅgaḥ saṃnipātaś ca maithune
english: The coming together with friends, the great arrival of wealth, the embrace of a son, and the union in conjugal love.

sanskrit: samaye ca priyālāpaḥ svayūtheṣu ca saṃnatiḥ abhipretasya lābhaś ca pūjā ca janasaṃsadi
english: Sweet conversation at the right moment, reverence among one's own people, the attainment of what is desired, and honour in a public assembly.

sanskrit: navadvāram idaṃ veśma tristhūṇaṃ pañcasākṣikam kṣetrajñādhiṣṭhitaṃ vidvān yo veda sa paraḥ kaviḥ
english: This dwelling of nine gates, supported by three pillars, witnessed by five, presided over by the knower of the field — he who knows it is the supreme sage.

sanskrit: daśa dharmaṃ na jānanti dhṛtarāṣṭra nibodha tān mattaḥ pramatta unmattaḥ śrāntaḥ kruddho bubhukṣitaḥ
english: Ten do not know dharma, O Dhṛtarāṣṭra — hear them: the intoxicated, the heedless, the mad, the exhausted, the angry, the hungry.

sanskrit: tvaramāṇaś ca bhīruś ca lubdhaḥ kāmī ca te daśa tasmād eteṣu bhāveṣu na prasajjeta paṇḍitaḥ
english: The one in haste, the coward, the greedy, and the lustful — those are the ten. Therefore a wise man should not fall into these states.

sanskrit: atraivodāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam putrārtham asurendreṇa gītaṃ caiva sudhanvanā
english: On this very point they cite this ancient tale, the song sung by the lord of the asuras, Sudhanvan, for the sake of his son.

sanskrit: yaḥ kāmamanyū prajahāti rājā; pātre pratiṣṭhāpayate dhanaṃ ca viśeṣavic chrutavān kṣiprakārī; taṃ sarvalokaḥ kurute pramāṇam
english: The king who abandons desire and anger, who places wealth in a worthy vessel, who is discerning, learned, and swift in action — him all the world regards as an authority.

sanskrit: jānāti viśvāsayituṃ manuṣyān; vijñātadoṣeṣu dadhāti daṇḍam jānāti mātrāṃ ca tathā kṣamāṃ ca; taṃ tādṛśaṃ śrīr juṣate samagrā
english: He knows how to inspire confidence in people; on those whose faults are known he inflicts punishment; he knows both measure and forbearance — such a one is graced by Śrī in her fullness.

sanskrit: sudurbalaṃ nāvajānāti kaṃ cid; yukto ripuṃ sevate buddhipūrvam na vigrahaṃ rocayate balasthaiḥ; kāle ca yo vikramate sa dhīraḥ
english: He does not despise even the very weak; vigilant, he manages his enemy with forethought; he does not relish conflict with the powerful; yet he who acts with valour at the right time — he is the wise one.

sanskrit: prāpyāpadaṃ na vyathate kadā cid; udyogam anvicchati cāpramattaḥ duḥkhaṃ ca kāle sahate jitātmā; dhuraṃdharas tasya jitāḥ sapatnāḥ
english: Having encountered calamity, he is never shaken; vigilant, he seeks out effort; the self-conqueror endures suffering in its time — the burden-bearer whose enemies are thus vanquished.

sanskrit: anarthakaṃ vipravāsaṃ gṛhebhyaḥ; pāpaiḥ saṃdhiṃ paradārābhimarśam dambhaṃ stainyaṃ paiśunaṃ madyapānaṃ; na sevate yaḥ sa sukhī sadaiva
english: Fruitless absence from home, alliance with the wicked, violation of another's wife, deceit, theft, slander, drinking wine — he who does not resort to these is always happy.

sanskrit: na saṃrambheṇārabhate 'rthavargam; ākāritaḥ śaṃsati tathyam eva na mātrārthe rocayate vivādaṃ; nāpūjitaḥ kupyati cāpy amūḍhaḥ
english: He does not undertake enterprises in anger; when asked, he speaks only the truth; he does not relish dispute over a trivial matter; nor, when not honoured, does the undeluded one grow angry.

sanskrit: na yo 'bhyasūyaty anukampate ca; na durbalaḥ prātibhāvyaṃ karoti nātyāha kiṃ cit kṣamate vivādaṃ; sarvatra tādṛg labhate praśaṃsām
english: He who neither envies nor lacks compassion; who, when weak, does not act as guarantor; who says nothing excessive and tolerates dispute — such a one wins praise everywhere.

sanskrit: yo noddhataṃ kurute jātu veṣaṃ; na pauruṣeṇāpi vikatthate 'nyān na mūrcchitaḥ kaṭukāny āha kiṃ cit; priyaṃ sadā taṃ kurute jano 'pi
english: He who never adopts an arrogant demeanour; who does not boast over others even of his own valour; who even when overcome says nothing harsh — people always hold such a one dear.

sanskrit: na vairam uddīpayati praśāntaṃ; na darpam ārohati nāstam eti na durgato 'smīti karoti manyuṃ; tam āryaśīlaṃ param āhur agryam
english: He does not rekindle an enmity that has been pacified; he does not rise to arrogance nor sink to abasement; he does not harbour anger saying 'I am in distress' — him they call foremost, the one of noble character.

sanskrit: na sve sukhe vai kurute praharṣaṃ; nānyasya duḥkhe bhavati pratītaḥ dattvā na paścāt kurute 'nutāpaṃ; na katthate satpuruṣāryaśīlaḥ
english: He truly does not exult in his own happiness; he is not pleased at another's suffering; having given, he does not afterwards repent — the good man of noble character does not boast.

sanskrit: deśācārān samayāñ jātidharmān; bubhūṣate yas tu parāvarajñaḥ sa tatra tatrādhigataḥ sadaiva; mahājanasyādhipatyaṃ karoti
english: He who, knowing high and low, seeks to honour the customs of the land, the conventions of the time, and the duties of caste — he, wherever he goes, always exercises lordship over the multitude.

sanskrit: dambhaṃ mohaṃ matsaraṃ pāpakṛtyaṃ; rājadviṣṭaṃ paiśunaṃ pūgavairam mattonmattair durjanaiś cāpi vādaṃ; yaḥ prajñāvān varjayet sa pradhānaḥ
english: Hypocrisy, delusion, envy, wicked deeds, what is hateful to kings, slander, enmity with groups, and dispute with the intoxicated, the mad, and the wicked — the prudent man who avoids these is foremost.

sanskrit: damaṃ śaucaṃ daivataṃ maṅgalāni; prāyaścittaṃ vividhāṃl lokavādān etāni yaḥ kurute naityakāni; tasyotthānaṃ devatā rādhayanti
english: Self-restraint, purity, worship of the gods, auspicious rites, expiation, and the various observances of the world — he who performs these daily: the gods prosper his undertakings.

sanskrit: samair vivāhaṃ kurute na hīnaiḥ; samaiḥ sakhyaṃ vyavahāraṃ kathāś ca guṇair viśiṣṭāṃś ca purodadhāti; vipaścitas tasya nayāḥ sunītāḥ
english: He contracts marriage with equals, not with inferiors; with equals he maintains friendship, dealings, and conversation; and he places before him those distinguished by virtue — the policies of such a wise man are truly well-guided.

sanskrit: mitaṃ bhuṅkte saṃvibhajyāśritebhyo; mitaṃ svapity amitaṃ karma kṛtvā dadāty amitreṣv api yācitaḥ saṃs; tam ātmavantaṃ prajahaty anarthāḥ
english: He eats moderately, having distributed to his dependants; he sleeps moderately though his work is immeasurable; being asked, he gives even to enemies — misfortunes forsake that self-possessed man.

sanskrit: cikīrṣitaṃ viprakṛtaṃ ca yasya; nānye janāḥ karma jānanti kiṃ cit mantre gupte samyag anuṣṭhite ca; svalpo nāsya vyathate kaś cid arthaḥ
english: He whose intended and accomplished deeds no other persons know at all, whose counsel, once kept secret and properly executed — no affair of his, however small, goes amiss.

sanskrit: yaḥ sarvabhūtapraśame niviṣṭaḥ; satyo mṛdur dānakṛc chuddhabhāvaḥ atīva saṃjñāyate jñātimadhye; mahāmaṇir jātya iva prasannaḥ
english: He who is devoted to the peace of all beings, truthful, gentle, generous, and pure of heart — he shines out exceedingly among his kinsmen, like a great gem of purest breed, radiant.

sanskrit: ya ātmanāpatrapate bhṛśaṃ naraḥ; sa sarvalokasya gurur bhavaty uta anantatejāḥ sumanāḥ samāhitaḥ; svatejasā sūrya ivāvabhāsate
english: The man who is deeply ashamed before himself becomes the teacher of all the world; of infinite lustre, cheerful of mind, composed — he shines by his own radiance like the sun.

sanskrit: vane jātāḥ śāpadagdhasya rājñaḥ; pāṇḍoḥ putrāḥ pañca pañcendrakalpāḥ tvayaiva bālā vardhitāḥ śikṣitāś ca; tavādeśaṃ pālayanty āmbikeya
english: Born in the forest, the sons of King Pāṇḍu — that king consumed by a curse — those five, each equal to Indra, were raised and trained by you yourself as children, O son of Ambikā; they abide by your command.

sanskrit: pradāyaiṣām ucitaṃ tāta rājyaṃ; sukhī putraiḥ sahito modamānaḥ na devānāṃ nāpi ca mānuṣāṇāṃ; bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ tarkaṇīyo narendra
english: Having given them their rightful kingdom, O father, you shall live happy, rejoicing with your sons; neither among the gods nor among men, O lord of kings, shall you be found wanting.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca jāgrato dahyamānasya yat kāryam anupaśyasi tad brūhi tvaṃ hi nas tāta dharmārthakuśalaḥ śuciḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Tell me what course of action you perceive for one who is awake and burning with anxiety — for you, dear one, are our expert in dharma and worldly affairs, and you are pure.

sanskrit: tvaṃ māṃ yathāvad vidura praśādhi; prajñāpūrvaṃ sarvam ajātaśatroḥ yan manyase pathyam adīnasattva; śreyaskaraṃ brūhi tad vai kurūṇām
english: Instruct me properly, O Vidura; tell me with full wisdom everything concerning Ajātaśatru — whatever you consider wholesome, O man of undaunted spirit; speak what will bring welfare to the Kurus.

sanskrit: pāpāśaṅkī pāpam evānupaśyan; pṛcchāmi tvāṃ vyākulenātmanāham kave tan me brūhi sarvaṃ yathāvan; manīṣitaṃ sarvam ajātaśatroḥ
english: Fearing evil and seeing only evil, I ask you with a troubled mind, O sage. Tell me everything exactly as it is — everything that Ajātaśatru has in mind.

sanskrit: vidura uvāca śubhaṃ vā yadi vā pāpaṃ dveṣyaṃ vā yadi vā priyam apṛṣṭas tasya tad brūyād yasya necchet parābhavam
english: Vidura said: Whether it be good or evil, whether hateful or pleasing, one should speak that unasked to one whose ruin one does not wish.

sanskrit: tasmād vakṣyāmi te rājan bhavam icchan kurūn prati vacaḥ śreyaskaraṃ dharmyaṃ bruvatas tan nibodha me
english: Therefore, O king, wishing welfare for the Kurus, I shall speak to you words that are beneficial and righteous — hear them from me as I speak.

sanskrit: mithyopetāni karmāṇi sidhyeyur yāni bhārata anupāyaprayuktāni mā sma teṣu manaḥ kṛthāḥ
english: O Bharata, those deeds which, though falsely undertaken, might succeed without application of the proper means — do not set your mind upon them.

sanskrit: tathaiva yogavihitaṃ na sidhyet karma yan nṛpa upāyayuktaṃ medhāvī na tatra glapayen manaḥ
english: Likewise, O king, a deed ordained by application of means may still not succeed; the intelligent man should not weary his mind over that either.

sanskrit: anubandhān avekṣeta sānubandheṣu karmasu saṃpradhārya ca kurvīta na vegena samācaret
english: In undertakings that have consequences, one should consider those consequences; having deliberated, one should act — one should not proceed with haste.

sanskrit: anubandhaṃ ca saṃprekṣya vipākāṃś caiva karmaṇām utthānam ātmanaś caiva dhīraḥ kurvīta vā na vā
english: Having looked at the consequences and the fruits of actions, and at his own capacity to rise to the task, the steadfast man should act or not act accordingly.

sanskrit: yaḥ pramāṇaṃ na jānāti sthāne vṛddhau tathā kṣaye kośe janapade daṇḍe na sa rājye 'vatiṣṭhate
english: He who does not know the measure in matters of maintenance, growth and decline, treasury, subjects, and the rod of punishment — such a one does not endure in kingship.

sanskrit: yas tv etāni pramāṇāni yathoktāny anupaśyati yukto dharmārthayor jñāne sa rājyam adhigacchati
english: But he who observes these measures as described, engaged in the knowledge of dharma and worldly affairs — he attains to sovereignty.

sanskrit: na rājyaṃ prāptam ity eva vartitavyam asāṃpratam śriyaṃ hy avinayo hanti jarā rūpam ivottamam
english: One should not conduct oneself improperly merely because a kingdom has been obtained; for insolence destroys prosperity as old age destroys the finest beauty.

sanskrit: bhakṣyottamapraticchannaṃ matsyo baḍiśam āyasam rūpābhipātī grasate nānubandham avekṣate
english: The fish, rushing at the appearance of the thing, swallows the iron hook hidden beneath the finest bait, and does not look to the consequence.

sanskrit: yac chakyaṃ grasituṃ grasyaṃ grastaṃ pariṇamec ca yat hitaṃ ca pariṇāme yat tad adyaṃ bhūtim icchatā
english: What can be swallowed, what ought to be swallowed, what once swallowed will digest, and what is beneficial in its digestion — that is what the man who desires prosperity should consume.

sanskrit: vanaspater apakvāni phalāni pracinoti yaḥ sa nāpnoti rasaṃ tebhyo bījaṃ cāsya vinaśyati
english: He who plucks the unripe fruits of a tree obtains no juice from them, and the seed within is also destroyed.

sanskrit: yas tu pakvam upādatte kāle pariṇataṃ phalam phalād rasaṃ sa labhate bījāc caiva phalaṃ punaḥ
english: But he who takes the ripe fruit, mature in its season — from the fruit he obtains its juice, and from the seed he obtains fruit again.

sanskrit: yathā madhu samādatte rakṣan puṣpāṇi ṣaṭpadaḥ tadvad arthān manuṣyebhya ādadyād avihiṃsayā
english: Just as the bee gathers honey while protecting the flowers, so should one take what one needs from people without harming them.

sanskrit: puṣpaṃ puṣpaṃ vicinvīta mūlacchedaṃ na kārayet mālākāra ivārāme na yathāṅgārakārakaḥ
english: One should gather flower by flower and not cause the cutting of the root — like a garland-maker in a garden, not like the charcoal-burner.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu me syād idaṃ kṛtvā kiṃ nu me syād akurvataḥ iti karmāṇi saṃcintya kuryād vā puruṣo na vā
english: What will accrue to me from doing this? What will accrue to me from not doing it? — having thought through his actions in this way, a man should act or refrain from acting.

sanskrit: anārabhyā bhavanty arthāḥ ke cin nityaṃ tathāgatāḥ kṛtaḥ puruṣakāro 'pi bhaved yeṣu nirarthakaḥ
english: Some goals should never be undertaken, and come to nothing regardless; in such matters even human effort exerted proves fruitless.

sanskrit: kāṃś cid arthān naraḥ prājño laghumūlān mahāphalān kṣipram ārabhate kartuṃ na vighnayati tādṛśān
english: Certain goals — those of small cost but great fruit — a wise man swiftly undertakes to accomplish; he does not obstruct such endeavours.

sanskrit: ṛju paśyati yaḥ sarvaṃ cakṣuṣānupibann iva āsīnam api tūṣṇīkam anurajyanti taṃ prajāḥ
english: He who sees everything plainly, as if drinking it in with his eyes, even sitting in silence — the people become attached to him.

sanskrit: cakṣuṣā manasā vācā karmaṇā ca caturvidham prasādayati lokaṃ yaḥ taṃ loko 'nuprasīdati
english: He who pleases the world in these four ways — by eye, by mind, by speech, and by deed — the world in turn becomes gracious toward him.

sanskrit: yasmāt trasyanti bhūtāni mṛgavyādhān mṛgā iva sāgarāntām api mahīṃ labdhvā sa parihīyate
english: He from whom living beings shrink away, as deer shrink from a hunter — even having obtained the earth to the edge of the ocean, such a one falls away.

sanskrit: pitṛpaitāmahaṃ rājyaṃ prāptavān svena tejasā vāyur abhram ivāsādya bhraṃśayaty anaye sthitaḥ
english: He who has obtained the ancestral kingdom by his own power, yet stands in wickedness, scatters it away as the wind scatters a cloud.

sanskrit: dharmam ācarato rājñaḥ sadbhiś caritam āditaḥ vasudhā vasusaṃpūrṇā vardhate bhūtivardhanī
english: For the king who practises dharma following the conduct of the good from the beginning, the earth full of riches grows and multiplies in prosperity.

sanskrit: atha saṃtyajato dharmam adharmaṃ cānutiṣṭhataḥ pratisaṃveṣṭate bhūmir agnau carmāhitaṃ yathā
english: But for the one who abandons dharma and practises adharma, the earth shrinks back as a hide placed in fire shrinks.

sanskrit: ya eva yatnaḥ kriyate pararāṣṭrāvamardane sa eva yatnaḥ kartavyaḥ svarāṣṭraparipālane
english: Whatever effort is made in crushing the kingdom of another, that very same effort should be made in protecting one's own kingdom.

sanskrit: dharmeṇa rājyaṃ vindeta dharmeṇa paripālayet dharmamūlāṃ śriyaṃ prāpya na jahāti na hīyate
english: By dharma one should acquire a kingdom; by dharma one should protect it; having attained prosperity rooted in dharma, one does not abandon it nor is diminished.

sanskrit: apy unmattāt pralapato bālāc ca parisarpataḥ sarvataḥ sāram ādadyād aśmabhya iva kāñcanam
english: Even from a babbling madman or a crawling child, one should extract the essence from everywhere, as gold is extracted from stones.

sanskrit: suvyāhṛtāni sudhiyāṃ sukṛtāni tatas tataḥ saṃcinvan dhīra āsīta śilāhārī śilaṃ yathā
english: A steadfast man should sit gathering the well-spoken words and well-done deeds of the wise from here and there, as a gleaner gathers grain.

sanskrit: gandhena gāvaḥ paśyanti vedaiḥ paśyanti brāhmaṇāḥ cāraiḥ paśyanti rājānaś cakṣurbhyām itare janāḥ
english: Cows perceive by smell, brahmins perceive by the Vedas, kings perceive through spies, and other people perceive through their eyes.

sanskrit: bhūyāṃsaṃ labhate kleśaṃ yā gaur bhavati durduhā atha yā suduhā rājan naiva tāṃ vinayanty api
english: A cow that is hard to milk gets more suffering inflicted on her; but the cow that is easy to milk, O king, they do not discipline even at all.

sanskrit: yad ataptaṃ praṇamati na tat saṃtāpayanty api yac ca svayaṃ nataṃ dāru na tat saṃnāmayanty api
english: Wood that bends without being heated — they do not try to heat it either; and wood that is already bent of itself — they do not try to bend it either.

sanskrit: etayopamayā dhīraḥ saṃnameta balīyase indrāya sa praṇamate namate yo balīyase
english: By this analogy, the wise man should bend toward the stronger — he who bows to the stronger bows, as it were, to Indra.

sanskrit: parjanyanāthāḥ paśavo rājāno mitrabāndhavāḥ patayo bāndhavāḥ strīṇāṃ brāhmaṇā vedabāndhavāḥ
english: Cattle have rain as their lord; kings have friends and kinsmen; husbands are the kinsmen of women; the Vedas are the kinsmen of brahmins.

sanskrit: satyena rakṣyate dharmo vidyā yogena rakṣyate mṛjayā rakṣyate rūpaṃ kulaṃ vṛttena rakṣyate
english: Dharma is protected by truth; learning is protected by practice; beauty is protected by cleanliness; lineage is protected by conduct.

sanskrit: mānena rakṣyate dhānyam aśvān rakṣaty anukramaḥ abhīkṣṇadarśanād gāvaḥ striyo rakṣyāḥ kucelataḥ
english: Grain is protected by proper storage; horses are protected by orderly exercise; cows are protected by frequent inspection; women are protected by plain clothing.

sanskrit: na kulaṃ vṛttahīnasya pramāṇam iti me matiḥ antyeṣv api hi jātānāṃ vṛttam eva viśiṣyate
english: Lineage is no authority for one devoid of good conduct — such is my view; for even among those born in the lowest station, conduct itself is what is distinguished.

sanskrit: ya īrṣyuḥ paravitteṣu rūpe vīrye kulānvaye sukhe saubhāgyasatkāre tasya vyādhir anantakaḥ
english: He who is envious of another's wealth, beauty, valour, lineage, happiness, good fortune, and honour — his disease is without end.

sanskrit: akāryakaraṇād bhītaḥ kāryāṇāṃ ca vivarjanāt akāle mantrabhedāc ca yena mādyen na tat pibet
english: That by which one should not be intoxicated — one should not drink it: from fear of doing what should not be done, from abandoning what should be done, and from untimely betrayal of counsel.

sanskrit: vidyāmado dhanamadas tṛtīyo 'bhijano madaḥ ete madāvaliptānām eta eva satāṃ damāḥ
english: Intoxication by learning, intoxication by wealth, and thirdly intoxication by noble birth — these are the three intoxications of the puffed-up, and these very same things are the self-disciplines of the good.

sanskrit: asanto 'bhyarthitāḥ sadbhiḥ kiṃ cit kāryaṃ kadā cana manyante santam ātmānam asantam api viśrutam
english: The ignoble, when asked by the noble to do any task at any time, think of themselves as virtuous even while being ignoble and of ill repute.

sanskrit: gatir ātmavatāṃ santaḥ santa eva satāṃ gatiḥ asatāṃ ca gatiḥ santo na tv asantaḥ satāṃ gatiḥ
english: The good are the refuge of the self-possessed; the good themselves are the refuge of the good; the good are also the refuge of the ignoble — but the ignoble are not the refuge of the good.

sanskrit: jitā sabhā vastravatā samāśā gomatā jitā adhvā jito yānavatā sarvaṃ śīlavatā jitam
english: The assembly is conquered by the well-dressed; equal hope is conquered by the one who has cattle; the road is conquered by the one who has a vehicle; everything is conquered by the one of good character.

sanskrit: śīlaṃ pradhānaṃ puruṣe tad yasyeha praṇaśyati na tasya jīvitenārtho na dhanena na bandhubhiḥ
english: Character is foremost in a man; for one in whom it perishes here, there is no use for him in life, nor in wealth, nor in kinsmen.

sanskrit: āḍhyānāṃ māṃsaparamaṃ madhyānāṃ gorasottaram lavaṇottaraṃ daridrāṇāṃ bhojanaṃ bharatarṣabha
english: For the wealthy the highest food is meat; for those of middling means the best is dairy produce; for the destitute, O bull of the Bharatas, salt is what tops their meal.

sanskrit: saṃpannataram evānnaṃ daridrā bhuñjate sadā kṣut svādutāṃ janayati sā cāḍhyeṣu sudurlabhā
english: The poor always eat food that is in fact more excellent; for hunger produces sweetness, and that sweetness is very hard to obtain among the rich.

sanskrit: prāyeṇa śrīmatāṃ loke bhoktuṃ śaktir na vidyate daridrāṇāṃ tu rājendra api kāṣṭhaṃ hi jīryate
english: In the world, the prosperous generally lack the capacity to enjoy food; but for the poor, O lord of kings, even wood is digested.

sanskrit: avṛttir bhayam antyānāṃ madhyānāṃ maraṇād bhayam uttamānāṃ tu martyānām avamānāt paraṃ bhayam
english: For the lowest, the greatest fear is loss of livelihood; for those of middling station, the fear is of death; but for the highest among mortals, the greatest fear is dishonour.
